old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a smoldering fire, focusing on the embers and smoke. The scene is set against a dark background, which contrasts sharply with the bright red-orange hues of the glowing embers at the bottom right corner. As the video progresses, wisps of white smoke rise from the center of the frame, billowing outward and partially obscuring the view of the fire. The smoke appears thick and dense, creating a dynamic interplay between light and shadow. The texture of the embers is rough and uneven, with some parts appearing charred and blackened, while others retain a reddish glow. The overall atmosphere is one of warmth and intensity, with the fire's glow providing a stark contrast to the surrounding darkness. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, maintaining a consistent focus on the fire and smoke, allowing viewers to observe the subtle changes in the smoke's movement and the embers' glow.

caption: The video captures a macro view of pale white smoke drifting and curling around a dark, roughly vertical object studded with small light-colored flaky fragments. The smoke is the dominant moving element, continuously changing shape and density as it rises and swirls past the object rather than translating as a single block. At several points a brighter, more opaque white puff wells up on the left side of the object before thinning and dispersing into the haze. The degree to which the smoke veils the central object varies over time, sometimes partly obscuring it and sometimes letting its dark surface and flakes show through. The solid object itself holds essentially the same position from first frame to last, without observable translation or rotation, while blurred diagonal lines remain in the dim background at the left. A steady red glow sits at the lower-right corner throughout, unchanging in location and brightness. The swirling motion is already underway at the opening and continues without resolution to the close, leaving the process visibly in progress at both ends.

infer a physical error from their mismatch, or manufacture continuity across a visible edit.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.

replace it with a short keyword prompt, physics explanation, checklist or a generic summary.

Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
